What To Do After a Motorcycle Accident in Greeley?

The first minutes and hours after a motorcycle accident in Greeley shape the strength of your claim, and the actions taken during that window are usually the ones an insurance company scrutinizes most closely later.
The following steps can help protect both your health and your case:
Seek Medical Care First:
Get checked even if you feel fine.
Road rash
or a jolted shoulder can mask deeper trauma that only surfaces once the adrenaline fades.
Report the Crash:
requires drivers to report accidents that cause injury or significant property damage. Ask for a copy of the report once officers document the scene and collect statements.
File a Report Yourself If No Officer Responds:
According to the
Colorado Department of Revenue
, you can file a report online. This counter report becomes part of the official record even without an officer present.
Photograph Everything:
Capture the bike, the road surface, and any visible injuries before the evidence fades.
Collect Witness Information:
If possible, get names and numbers on the scene. Insurers often lean on independent accounts when your version of events is challenged.
Call a Greeley Accident Lawyer:
Bring in legal help early to preserve evidence and protect the deadlines your claim depends on.
Each of these steps builds toward the same goal, a claim that stands on solid documentation rather than on what an adjuster assumes happened.
What Compensation Can You Get from a Motorcycle Accident Claim?
A
motorcycle accident claim in Colorado
can include several categories of compensation. Understanding each one helps you recognize what a fair
settlement
should reflect.
Economic damages cover the direct costs of your crash, including:
Emergency treatment and surgery
Physical therapy
Wages lost during recovery
Reduced future earning capacity, when injuries limit your ability to work
Non-economic damages address the harder to quantify effects of a crash, treated separately under
Colorado’s civil jury instructions
, including:
Pain and suffering
Emotional distress
Reduced quality of life following a serious injury

Property damage covers the repair or replacement of your motorcycle, along with any gear damaged in the crash, and, in cases involving especially reckless conduct, Colorado law may also allow punitive damages, intended to punish the responsible party rather than compensate the victim.

Every claim depends on its own facts. A fractured wrist and two weeks of missed work call for a different calculation than a spinal injury requiring months of rehabilitation, and fault plays just as large a role in that calculation as the injury itself.
Contributory Negligence in Greeley, Colorado
Insurance companies frequently try to shift blame onto the motorcyclist after a crash, arguing that you were speeding,
lane splitting
, or otherwise responsible for what happened. Colorado’s modified comparative negligence law,
, directly addresses these situations.

You can still recover money even if you share some of the blame, as long as your share stays below 50 percent. Whatever percentage you are assigned gets subtracted from your payout. A rider found 20 percent at fault, for example, could still walk away with 80 percent of the total damages awarded.

Adjusters know this rule well, and many push hard on comparative fault to shrink what they owe you. Dashcam footage, witness statements, and accident reconstruction can push back on an unfair number. A
Greeley motorcycle accident lawyer
can review these details before any fault percentage gets locked in, since an early, inaccurate assignment can significantly reduce the value of your claim.
Common Causes of Motorcycle Accidents in Greeley
Motorcycle accidents in Greeley trace back to a familiar set of causes, many of which reflect a failure by other drivers to share the road safely:
Left-turn collisions, when a driver misjudges a motorcycle’s speed or distance while turning across traffic
Distracted driving, where a glance at a phone for even 2 seconds can miss a motorcyclist entirely
Failure to check blind spots during a lane change, since a motorcycle’s smaller profile makes it easy to overlook
Gravel, potholes, and uneven pavement, which pose a far greater danger to a rider balancing on two wheels than to a car or truck
Speeding, whether by the rider or another driver, which shortens the window for a safe reaction and increases the severity of injuries when a crash occurs
These causes rarely exist in isolation, and they tend to concentrate on the same stretches of road throughout Weld County year after year.
Motorcycle Accident Injuries in Greeley
Motorcyclists face a level of exposure most drivers never experience, and the injuries that follow a crash often reflect that lack of protection:
Traumatic brain injuries, ranging from concussions to more severe, long-term cognitive impairment
Spinal cord injuries, which can result in partial or complete paralysis
Fractures and broken bones, especially in the arms, legs, and ribs
Road rash,
caused by sliding across pavement, which can require skin grafts and leave permanent scarring
Internal injuries, which are not always obvious right away, can worsen without prompt treatment
These injuries often carry long recovery timelines and high medical costs, and our

Dormer Harpring

Dangerous Roads in Greeley for Motorcycle Riders
Certain roads around Greeley present heightened risks for motorcyclists, largely due to traffic volume, speed, and the mix of vehicles sharing the corridor:
U.S. Highway 85:
Heavy commercial and commuter traffic runs south through Weld County, and higher speeds combined with frequent lane changes create real hazards for riders.
U.S. Highway 34:

East of Greeley, agricultural equipment shares the road with commuter vehicles along long straightaways that can tempt speeding. Riders crossing intersections here face particular risk from drivers who misjudge a motorcycle’s speed at a distance.
County Roads Throughout Weld County:
These carry heavy local traffic alongside drivers cutting through toward Greeley’s commercial districts, and some stretches lack the shoulder space a rider needs to avoid a sudden hazard.
Corridors Near Busier Shopping Areas:
Sections of 35th Avenue experience frequent congestion, which increases the likelihood that a distracted or rushed driver will miss a motorcyclist entirely.
Knowing which roads carry the greatest risk will not prevent every crash, but it helps identify how a crash likely happened. A
Greeley motorcycle accident lawyer
familiar with these corridors can use that context to challenge assumptions about fault before they become the final word on your claim.

faqs.question: How long do I have to file a motorcycle accident claim in Colorado?

children.text: Colorado generally allows three years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury claim. Certain exceptions can shorten or extend this window, so it is worth confirming your specific deadline early rather than assuming you have more time than you do. Waiting too long can bar your right to recover compensation entirely.

faqs.question: Will I still have a case if I was not wearing a helmet?

children.text: Colorado does not require adult riders to wear a helmet, so going without one does not automatically bar your claim. An insurer may still try to use it as a factor in a comparative fault argument, which is one more reason to have a
Greeley motorcycle accident lawyer
review your case before accepting any settlement offer.

faqs.question: What happens if the other driver did not have insurance?

children.text: If the at-fault driver was uninsured or underinsured, your own policy’s uninsured or underinsured motorist coverage may become the primary source of compensation. Reviewing your policy early can help clarify what coverage is available to you.

faqs.question: How long does a motorcycle accident claim usually take to resolve?

children.text: Timelines vary depending on the severity of your injuries, whether liability is disputed, and how willing the insurer is to negotiate in good faith. Straightforward cases with clear fault can be resolved in months, while more serious injuries often take longer because the full cost of recovery must be understood before a fair settlement is possible.

faqs.question: Will my case go to trial, or does it typically settle?

children.text: Most motorcycle accident claims settle before trial, but the outcome depends on whether the insurer offers a fair amount once your damages are fully documented. At
Dormer Harpring
, we prepare every case for trial if a fair settlement is not offered, since this willingness often affects how seriously an insurer negotiates.
